There's a meeting about sustainability on campus at the UPC. Laia is on the organising team and asks you what bothers you and what you suggest.
Say what bothers you and what pleases you with me molesta / me alegra que + subj., and make suggestions with es importante / necesario que + subj.
me alegra que · me molesta que

For feelings about something that someone else does, use the subjunctive:

FeelingExample
me alegra queMe alegra que vengas.
me molesta queMe molesta que la gente tire basura.
me preocupa queMe preocupa que no llueva.
me encanta / odio queMe encanta que haga sol.
Same person → infinitive: Me alegra verte. (I'm happy – I see you.) But: Me alegra que me veas.
It bothers me that they don't recycle in the office.
I'm glad you came. (that you're coming)
I love that there are so many bikes in Barcelona.
es importante que · es una pena que

general: infinitivewith a person: que + subj.
Es importante reciclar.Es importante que reciclemos.
Es necesario ahorrar agua.Es necesario que todos ahorren agua.
Es una pena tirar comida.Es una pena que la gente tire comida.

Also: es normal / lógico / increíble / mejor / fundamental que …

But facts → indicative: Es verdad / Es obvio que hace calor.
It's a shame you can't come.
Laia is chairing the meeting and asks you directly.
Jonas, you're from Germany – what bothers you here on campus?
True. And what do you suggest?
Great idea! I'll write it down.
It's essential that we all save water, especially in summer.

Rule of thumb: fact → indicative. Wish, doubt, feeling, future, the unknown → subjunctive.

Este verano, Cataluña ha vivido una de las peores sequías de su historia. En muchos pueblos se ha prohibido llenar piscinas y regar los jardines. En Barcelona, las fuentes de los parques se han apagado.

«Me preocupa que la gente no se tome en serio el problema», dice Jordi, un agricultor de la zona. «Es necesario que todos cambiemos nuestros hábitos: duchas más cortas, menos agua en el jardín». Los expertos creen que las sequías serán cada vez más frecuentes. Por eso, es importante que las ciudades {inviertan|invest} en reciclar el agua. Lo bueno es que muchos jóvenes ya están {concienciados|aware, conscious}: el consumo de agua en los hogares ha bajado un 10 %.

This summer Catalonia went through one of the worst droughts in its history. In many villages it was forbidden to fill swimming pools and water gardens. In Barcelona the fountains in the parks were switched off.

"It worries me that people don't take the problem seriously," says Jordi, a farmer from the area. "We all need to change our habits: shorter showers, less water in the garden." Experts believe droughts will become more and more frequent. That's why it's important for cities to invest in recycling water. The good news is that many young people are already aware: water consumption in households has fallen by 10%.
